extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans, and researchers seeking biographical and career information about a comedian
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia biography summarizing the life, career, genres, influences, roles, and achievements of comedian and actor Patton Oswalt. It documents his mediums, recurring subjects, notable works, and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genres
rubrics_metrics.description: Observational comedy; black comedy; insult comedy; sarcasm; satire; deadpan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in the article's infobox as the primary comedic genres associated with Patton Oswalt; serves as descriptive labels for the style(s) of material he performs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: American culture; American politics; human behavior; pop culture; current events; religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named in the infobox as recurring subject matter in Oswalt's comedy and writing, indicating typical thematic territory for his routines and public commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medium
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows the primary performance and distribution media Oswalt works in — useful for understanding where his comedic work appears (live stand-up, TV roles/narration, film and voice acting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Range of stand-up topics (frivolous to serious)
rubrics_metrics.description: Oswalt's stand-up comedy covers topics ranging from pop culture frivolity, such as comic book supervillains and 1980s glam metal, to deeper social issues like American excess, materialism, foreign policy, and religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the breadth of tone and subject matter in his material — a model for balancing light, pop-culture jokes with socially engaged or serious content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal beliefs and experiences in material
rubrics_metrics.description: He also discusses his atheism in his stand-up. Oswalt has been diagnosed with clinical depression, which he has dealt with throughout his adult life. He has incorporated these experiences into his comedy routines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates an approach where personal conviction and life experiences are used as source material; suggests authenticity and vulnerability as elements in his comedic voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influences
rubrics_metrics.description: Oswalt's influences include Jonathan Winters, Richard Pryor, Emo Philips, Blaine Capatch, Jim Goad, Bill Hicks, Bobcat Goldthwait, Sam Kinison, Steve Martin, and Louis C.K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists notable comedians who shaped his style and sensibility; useful for situating his work in a lineage of comedic approaches (e.g., observational, confrontational, surreal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of diverse performance types (voice acting, roasts, panel moderation, writing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Oswalt has voiced characters in animated films and series (Remy in Ratatouille; characters in BoJack Horseman, The Secret Life of Pets 2, M.O.D.O.K.), appeared in roast comedy, moderated panels (Mystery Science Theater 3000 reunion), and written books and comics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents diversification of comedic career beyond stand-up — voice work, roasts, writing, and moderation — illustrating multiple outlets and formats for comedic work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recorded specials and distribution platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Notable specials/albums include Patton Oswalt: My Weakness Is Strong (Comedy Central), Talking for Clapping (Netflix), Tragedy Plus Comedy Equals Time (Epix/Comedy Central), Annihilation (Netflix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows platforms and formats (TV special, Netflix special, albums, DVDs) where his comedy is packaged and distributed; useful as indicators of reach and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and recognition as quality indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Oswalt won a Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Writing for a Variety Special and a Grammy Award for Best Comedy Album for Talking for Clapping (2016). Numerous other nominations and awards are listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards and nominations are presented as evidence of industry recognition and achievement; can be used as objective indicators of success or impact within comedy and entertainment.
